newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Debre wants RPR leadership vote in July.
newsitem.headline: France's Debre wants RPR leadership vote in July.

text.p: A leader of France's defeated Gaullist party said on Thursday he wanted an emergency party congress brought forward to July to resolve a bitter leadership fight after the left swept to power in a parliamentary election.
"I would like the congress to take place in July," Jean-Louis Debre, the new interim secretary-general of the conservative Rally for the Republic party, told RMC radio.
Ousted prime minister Alain Juppe, president of the RPR, on Tuesday called the emergency congress for September to elect a new leader, but failed to still calls for his resignation.

Juppe has not spelt out if he will run again but has faced a barrage of calls to stand down immediately after the parliamentary election defeat on Sunday brought new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to power.
Many Gaullists want Juppe to stand down in favour of rival Philippe Seguin, the former National Assembly speaker.
"I'm among those who believe that, after a defeat, we must reflect, change structures, probably change leaders, but not any old way. We must do it responsibly, calmly, and with thought," Debre said.
Seguin, the former National Assembly speaker, took over the leadership of the right's election campaign at the last minute after Juppe bowed out following the first-round left-wing upset.
